newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians accuse Gingrich of "racist trash".
newsitem.headline: Palestinians accuse Gingrich of "racist trash".

text.p: A senior adviser to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat accused U.S. Republican Speaker Newt Gingrich on Wednesday of talking "racist trash" in his backing for action by Israel against Palestinian militants.

Ahmed Tibi said statements by some U.S. congressmen since two Arab suicide bombers killed 13 other people in a Jerusalem market last week sounded like they came from the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement of the late U.S.-born Rabbi Meir Kahane.
This was especially so in the case of Gingrich, the House of Representatives Speaker, said Tibi, an Israeli Arab.
"I think that the remarks of Mr Gingrich are racist, foolish and should be thrown into (the) trash," Tibi told foreign media.

Gingrich, one of America's most powerful politicians, directed fierce criticism at Arafat on Sunday and said he backed whatever steps Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu needed to impose to protect Israeli citizens.
He said there was "clear evidence that Yasser Arafat and the Palestinian Authority have not only not stopped terrorism, but had people in their organisation helping terrorists."
The Palestinian Authority's Information Ministry, in a statement on Wednesday, said Gingrich's position "makes the extreme right wing in Israel look moderate".

"His statements regarding President Arafat are void of any truth, constitute an incitement against the peace process and certainly encourage the Netanyahu government to further destroy what is left of the peace process," the statement said.
Noting Israeli and Palestinian suspicions that the bombers might have come from abroad, it questioned Gingrich's credibility and accused him of lacking in objectivity.
"We in Palestine did not hear Gingrich protesting Israelis killing Palestinians in cold blood," the statement said.
Netanyahu has accused Arafat of doing "damn all" to halt violence by militants from Hamas and other Islamist groups opposed to the Jewish state's existence, a charge the Palestinian Authority denies.

Netanyahu has clamped an economic and security blockade on the West Bank and Gaza Strip, vowed to re-enter self-rule areas to snatch militants if Arafat fails to do the job and made a resumption of peace talks contingent on security cooperation from the Palestinian Authority.

Tibi accused Netanyahu of using the attack as an excuse to dismantle interim peace deals signed with the PLO by previous Labour governments, weaken Arafat's legitimacy and exact collective punishment on Palestinians.
He said calls to crush Hamas, in whose name last week's attack has been claimed, were "fascistic (and) anti-democratic".
The movement has an extended social welfare network in Palestinian areas and Tibi said it enjoyed substantial support.

"Nobody is allowed to ask Yasser Arafat to crush down part of his Palestinian people," Tibi said, adding that Palestinian police action was aimed at identifying those responsible for the bombings rather than at mass arrests.

Wednesday's attacks have sharpened doubts about whether Congress will renew approval for the U.S. administration to continue aid to the Palestinian Authority and contacts with the PLO when it returns from its summer recess.
